records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Europe
records.short_title: EU Communication on AI for Europe (2018)
records.summary: European Commission strategy for an EU initiative on AI in three parts: boosting the EU's technological and industrial capacity and AI uptake, aiming at public and private AI investment of at least EUR 20 billion by the end of 2020; preparing for socioeconomic changes; and ensuring an appropriate ethical and legal framework. Under that framework the Commission undertook to have draft AI ethics guidelines developed with stakeholders by the end of 2018, to issue guidance on the Product Liability Directive and a report on the liability and safety frameworks for AI, the Internet of Things and robotics by mid-2019, and to support research on explainable AI.
records.notes: Accompanied by a Commission staff working document on liability, SWD(2018) 137. The communication builds on the declaration of cooperation on AI signed on 10 April 2018 by 24 Member States and Norway, encourages every Member State to have an AI strategy, and announced a coordinated plan on AI with Member States by the end of 2018 and a European AI Alliance by July 2018. As a first step the Commission raised AI investment under Horizon 2020 to around EUR 1.5 billion for 2018-2020. It names safety and liability, security (criminal use or attacks), bias and discrimination among the risks of AI, says consumers should know whether they are communicating with a machine or another human, and says the Commission will review existing legal frameworks if necessary.
records.scope_note: Mainly a strategy for AI investment, research and uptake, with an ethical and legal framework as one of its three parts; included as the European Commission's first AI strategy, which launched the AI ethics guidelines and the review of the safety and liability rules for AI.

verification.note: Stored the Commission's PDF of COM(2018) 237 final from ec.europa.eu (20 pages), which confirms the title, the number, the date 'Brussels, 25.4.2018' and the content, and the Commission's library page on digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu with its printable PDF, which gives the publication date 25 April 2018. The candidate's EUR-Lex URL and the European Parliament register copy returned bot-check pages with no text. No stored source says the communication was withdrawn or replaced.

records.title: European Ethical Charter on the use of Artificial Intelligence in judicial systems and their environment
records.short_title: CEPEJ Ethical Charter on AI in judicial systems
records.issuing_body: European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice (CEPEJ), Council of Europe
records.summary: Charter adopted by the Council of Europe's European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice (CEPEJ) that sets five principles for AI tools and services processing judicial decisions and data: respect for fundamental rights, with ethical-by-design or human-rights-by-design approaches; non-discrimination; quality and security, with certified sources, traceable processing and secure environments; transparency, impartiality and fairness, with external audits and possible certification by independent authorities; and user control, so that justice professionals can review results and parties are told of AI processing and can object and have a court hear their case.
records.notes: Adopted at the CEPEJ's 31st plenary meeting in Strasbourg on 3-4 December 2018; the document is dated 3 December 2018. It is addressed to public and private stakeholders that design and deploy such tools and to public decision-makers responsible for the legislative or regulatory framework, and says the use of these tools in criminal matters must be considered with the greatest reservations to prevent discrimination based on sensitive data. The principles are to be applied, monitored and evaluated regularly, and independent authorities could periodically assess their endorsement. An in-depth study on the use of AI in judicial systems and a glossary are appended. Council of Europe Publishing issues it as a 79-page publication (2019).

verification.note: Stored the Council of Europe Publishing page for the charter on book.coe.int, which confirms the title, CEPEJ as author, the adoption on 4 December 2018, the five principles and the contents; book.coe.int counts as official through its .int domain. Also stored a full copy of the charter document CEPEJ(2018)14 from questionegiustizia.it (secondary: the site of an Italian legal journal), which gives the identifier, the plenary meeting and the full wording of the principles. The official PDF on rm.coe.int (https://rm.coe.int/ethical-charter-en-for-publication-4-december-2018/16808f699c, the candidate URL) answered 403 and is not stored; official_identifier, the notes on the addressees, criminal matters and application, and the details of the principles in the summary rest on the secondary copy until the official PDF is stored by a browser retry or provided as a document. records.title: Artificial Intelligence Strategy
records.summary: Strategy of the German Federal Government for AI research, transfer to industry, skills and use, backed by about EUR 3 billion of federal funding to 2025. Its three equal aims are making Germany and Europe a leading AI location, responsible and public-interest-oriented development and use of AI, and embedding AI ethically, legally, culturally and institutionally in society. It commits to review the legal framework for gaps in algorithmic and AI-based decisions, to examine how AI systems can be made transparent, traceable and verifiable, and to examine state bodies and private testing institutions to oversee algorithmic decisions, with audit and impact-assessment standards.
records.notes: Prepared under the joint lead of the Federal Ministries of Education and Research, for Economic Affairs and Energy, and of Labour and Social Affairs after a nationwide online consultation, on the basis of key points the Federal Cabinet adopted on 18 July 2018. The cabinet decided the strategy on 15 November 2018; it was transmitted to the Bundesrat (Drucksache 597/18) and the Bundestag (Drucksache 19/5880). Its other governance measures include an ethics by, in and for design approach, an aim of obliging hardware and software makers to follow security by design, raising the security of AI systems against attacks, research on detecting manipulated or automatically generated content, a German AI observatory, and a roadmap on AI norms and standards with DIN, including standardised classifications of the risks associated with AI. It plans to take up the recommendations of the Data Ethics Commission and to seek common guidelines in the OECD, G7, G20 and the United Nations. The cabinet adopted an update (Fortschreibung 2020) on 2 December 2020, which raised planned federal funding to 2025 from three to five billion euros and puts new weight on pandemic response, sustainability, environmental and climate protection, and international and European networking.
records.scope_note: Mainly a national strategy for AI research, transfer to industry, skills and funding, with its safety and risk-governance content in the sections on the regulatory framework, standards and IT security; included as the Federal Government's national AI strategy.

english_version.by: Federal Government of Germany (Federal Ministries of Education and Research, for Economic Affairs and Energy, and of Labour and Social Affairs)

records.title: AI for Humanity: national strategy for artificial intelligence
records.issuing_body: President of the Republic and Government of France
records.summary: France's national AI strategy, presented by the President on 29 March 2018 at the Collège de France on the basis of the Villani report, with 1.5 billion euros of public funding over the five-year term. Its pillars are the AI ecosystem and talent, with a national research programme coordinated by Inria; an active policy of opening data; a financing and regulatory framework for priority sectors such as health and mobility; and the ethical and political questions of AI. On ethics it calls for public transparency of algorithms, tracking their bias, not leaving them the monopoly of decisions, a European reflection on the control and certification of algorithms, and an IPCC-like body for AI.
records.notes: Presented at the 'AI for Humanity' conference; the government press kit of 28 November 2018 describes the strategy in three axes: talent, diffusion of AI in the economy and society, and ethics. The funding includes 100 million euros from the Fund for Innovation and Industry for AI start-ups, 70 million euros a year through the public investment bank for deep-technology start-ups and 400 million euros for innovation challenges and industrial projects, within a total of 1.5 billion euros of public money expected to bring more than 500 million euros of private investment. The President said the State would by default make public the code of all algorithms it uses, starting with Parcoursup, and announced a regulatory framework for autonomous vehicles by 2022. The national research strategy for AI of 28 November 2018 is its research component: a national programme run by Inria with interdisciplinary AI institutes (3IA), 40 chairs and a doubling of AI doctorates. A 'Grand Défi' launched on 18 July 2018 aims to secure, certify and make reliable systems that use AI.
records.scope_note: Mainly a strategy for AI research, talent, data and funding, with ethics as one of its pillars, and set out in the President's speech and government press material rather than in a single strategy document; included as France's national AI strategy.

verification.note: Stored the press kit of the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Innovation and the Secretary of State for Digital Affairs of 28 November 2018 from enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr (official), which confirms the presentation on 29 March 2018, the Government's mobilisation around the strategy, the funding and the three axes, and the Élysée's page and PDF of the President's speech of 29 March 2018, which give the four pillars and the ethics measures (the page also linked an unrelated deontology guide, which was stored). The English title renders the French one ('AI for Humanity' is the strategy's own name); no English text of the strategy is stored. The summary follows the French texts.

records.title: Charlevoix Common Vision for the Future of Artificial Intelligence
records.short_title: G7 Charlevoix Common Vision on AI (2018)
records.summary: Commitment by the G7 leaders at their 2018 Charlevoix summit to promote human-centric AI and its commercial adoption. They commit to safeguard privacy, invest in cybersecurity, promote industry research on safety, assurance, data quality and data security, encourage AI that addresses accountability, assurance, liability, security, safety, bias and potential misuse, foster initiatives that promote safety and transparency and give guidance on human intervention in AI decision-making, and improve digital security in AI through voluntary codes of conduct, standards or guidelines, alongside commitments on skills, gender equality and adoption by small firms.
records.notes: One of eight declarations the G7 leaders issued on 9 June 2018 at the 44th G7 summit in La Malbaie (Charlevoix), Quebec. It refers to the 2018 G7 Montreal Ministerial Statement on Artificial Intelligence and to the multi-stakeholder, human-centric vision of the 2017 G7 ICT and Industry Ministers' Torino Declaration. Its other commitments cover lifelong learning and reskilling, the participation of women and underrepresented groups, multistakeholder dialogue, support for unpaid caregivers, and an open and fair market environment including the free flow of information. Global Affairs Canada published it in English and in French (Vision commune de Charlevoix sur l'avenir de l'intelligence artificielle).

verification.note: Stored Global Affairs Canada's page with the full English text and its PDF version, the French page and PDF, and the Government of Canada Publications catalogue record (all on gc.ca, official). The text confirms the title and the commitments by 'the Leaders of the G7'; the catalogue record confirms the issue on 9 June 2018 at the Charlevoix summit (44th G7 summit, La Malbaie), the publisher and the French edition. The candidate's publications.gc.ca PDF link now leads to an archived-content notice with no text. A copy on mofa.go.jp refused a plain request and was not stored.

records.title: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
records.summary: Discussion paper by NITI Aayog that lays the groundwork for India's national AI strategy under the banner #AIforAll, focused on AI for social and inclusive growth in healthcare, agriculture, education, smart cities and infrastructure, and smart mobility and transportation. It proposes research centres, the AIRAWAT compute platform, skilling and data marketplaces. Its chapter on ethics, privacy and security addresses bias and explainability, calls for a data protection law and sector-specific guidelines, and proposes a negligence test for damage caused by AI, safe harbours where an AI product was properly designed, tested and monitored, and ethics councils at each research centre.
records.notes: NITI Aayog prepared the paper under the mandate in the Finance Minister's budget speech for 2018-19 to establish a National Program on AI. It leaves execution and financial details aside pending wider consultation and says its recommendations would need a significant budgetary allocation. It proposes Centres of Research Excellence (COREs) for core research and International Centres for Transformational AI (ICTAIs) for applied research, with ICTAI Inc. as an umbrella body, a 'CERN for AI', a task force on intellectual property, and a Centre for Studies on Technological Sustainability for ethical, privacy and legal questions. On liability it also proposes a framework for apportioning damages and an actual-harm requirement for lawsuits, and it says the accountability debate should shift to identifying the component that failed and how to prevent it in future. NITI Aayog's AIRAWAT approach paper of January 2020 dates the release to 4 June 2018; NITI's publication page for the paper shows a publication date of 27 June 2018.
records.scope_note: A discussion paper mainly on AI adoption, research and skilling in five sectors, with one chapter on ethics, privacy and security; included as India's first national AI strategy paper.

verification.note: Stored the NITI Aayog PDF from niti.gov.in (114 pages), NITI's publication page for it (node 708) and NITI's approach paper on AIRAWAT (January 2020). The paper confirms the title, NITI Aayog's authorship and mandate (foreword signed by its CEO), that it is a discussion paper, and its recommendations, including the chapter 'Ethics, Privacy, Security and Artificial Intelligence'. The paper itself carries no date and its cover has no text layer; date_published rests on the AIRAWAT paper ('released ... on 4th June, 2018'). NITI's publication page gives 'Wed, 06/27/2018', which looks like the date the item was posted on the site; the discrepancy is in the notes.
